The following is a history of the '''list of games played between NBA and international teams'''. Teams from the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) have played numerous [[basketball]] games against various international teams from around the world. NBA teams, from both the United States and Canada, have played many games against international [[sports club|clubs]] from various different [[List of basketball leagues|professional basketball leagues]], as well as against some league all-star teams and senior [[national sports team|national teams]].

==History==
One of the first [[basketball]] games between an [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] and an international team was held in 1978, in [[Tel Aviv]], [[Israel]]. [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]] of the [[EuroLeague]] and [[Israeli Basketball Premier League|Israeli League]] surprisingly beat the defending [[NBA champion]]s, the [[Washington Bullets]], by a score of 98–97.<ref>[http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=5634 Expedientes X (I)]; ACB.com 31 July 2002 {{in lang|es}}</ref>

Since then, six other [[EuroLeague]] teams have defeated an [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] franchise: [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|Barcelona]], [[CB Málaga|Málaga]] and [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] from the [[Liga ACB|Spanish League]], [[PBC CSKA Moscow|CSKA Moscow]] of the Russian top-tier level [[VTB United League]], [[Fenerbahçe Men's Basketball|Fenerbahçe]] from the [[Turkish Basketball Super League|Turkish League]], and [[Alba Berlin]] from the [[Basketball Bundesliga|German League]].

In addition to defeating the [[Washington Bullets]] in 1978, [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]] also beat the [[New Jersey Nets]] and [[Phoenix Suns]] in 1984, in Israel, and beat the [[Toronto Raptors]], 103–105, in [[Toronto]] in 2005. This was the first loss of an NBA team on North American soil.

The first Barcelona and CSKA wins came during the [[2006 NBA Europe Live Tour]], where Barcelona beat the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] 104–99, and the Moscow team won by 19 over the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] (94–75), being the widest victory so far of any international team.

During the [[2007 NBA Europe Live Tour]], [[CB Málaga|Málaga]] defeated [[Memphis Grizzlies]] 102–99, and [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] overcame [[Toronto Raptors|Toronto]] by a narrow 104–103. In 2010, Barcelona and CSKA Moscow again, beat NBA teams, by narrow margins. More recent EuroLeague victories came during the [[2012 NBA Europe Live Tour]], when [[Fenerbahçe Men's Basketball|Fenerbahçe]] defeated the [[Boston Celtics]], by a score of 97–91, and Barcelona beat the [[Dallas Mavericks]], by a score of 99–85. In 2013, CSKA beat the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] by a score of 108–106, and in 2014, [[Alba Berlin]] beat the [[San Antonio Spurs]] by a score of 94–93. In 2016, [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] beat the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] in [[overtime (sports)|overtime]], by a score of 142–137.

Many of these games were initially played as part of the now-defunct [[McDonald's Championship]], which NBA teams win all of the editions. After 2006, they were mostly played during the [[NBA Europe Live Tour]] and the [[EuroLeague American Tour]]. In addition to the EuroLeague teams that have beaten NBA teams, one senior men's European [[national sports team|national team]], the [[Soviet Union men's national basketball team|Soviet Union]], beat the [[Atlanta Hawks]], by a score of 132–123, in an [[friendly game|exhibition game]] in Moscow, in 1988.

So far, only one non-European team has beaten an NBA team (Israeli teams participate in European competitions). The [[Adelaide 36ers]], a team from the [[National Basketball League (Australia)|NBL]], which is the top-tier professional league of Australia and New Zealand, beat the [[Phoenix Suns]], by a score 134–124, in 2022.
